standout_why: Compared against the two pages I could open: dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam (cited in chat 1) and dashlore.com/guides/best-dash-cams. Our page says the Vantrue N5S, Rexing R4 and Rexing C4 need a hardwire kit sold separately but gives no kit price and no total, and states no frame rate for any model. Dashlore covers only the N5S (30 fps on all four channels, kit sold separately, no price). The Rexing R4-RD maker page (a result in chat 2) returned HTTP 429, but its store record says the kit is included without comparing against anything. ChatGPT's own answer repeats 'included hardwire kit' for the R4-RD and a Botslab bundle but never totals the others. Capped at 2 because I could not get the per-channel frame rates for Rexing, REDTIGER or Botslab from maker pages (botslab.com, redtigercam.com, vantrue.com and rexing.com product pages all returned HTTP 429/0), so the table is incomplete.
decides: It splits the $300 line in two. As a driving recorder the Vantrue N5S ($293.99) is under budget and is the only candidate whose maker names STARVIS 2 on all four cameras, with all four channels at 30 fps per Dashlore; that confirms it for rideshare and cabin use. Ready for parking mode, the N5S is $328.98 and the Vantrue N5 is $300.98 with Vantrue's $34.99 kit, both over $300. The Rexing R4 with Rexing's $39.99 kit is $299.98. The Rexing R4-RD at $279.99 has the kit in the box and is the only parking-ready front/rear/left/right camera under $300 that I could confirm from a maker record today. The Botslab G980H (ours) would win that segment on price only if its listing includes the hardwire kit, which I could not open to verify.
